# AEW All Out 2021

**Date:** September 5, 2021

**Venue:** NOW Arena (formerly known as the Sears Centre) in Hoffman Estates, Illinois (suburban Chicago)

**Promotion:** All Elite Wrestling (AEW)

## Significance

All Out 2021 is widely regarded as one of the most important events in AEW history and one of the most memorable professional wrestling pay-per-views in years. It was highlighted by several major debuts that sent shockwaves through the wrestling world.

## Major Debuts

The event became legendary largely because of the debuts of several high-profile former WWE stars:

- **Adam Cole** – debuted after the main event, aligning with The Elite
- **Bryan Danielson** (Daniel Bryan) – debuted after the main event, confronting Kenny Omega and The Elite
- **Ruby Soho** (Ruby Riott) – debuted as a surprise entrant and won the Casino Battle Royale
- **Minoru Suzuki** – appeared to confront Jon Moxley

## Match Card & Results

### Main Event
- **Kenny Omega (c) vs. Christian Cage** – AEW World Championship – Omega retained

### Other Key Matches
- **Dr. Britt Baker D.M.D. (c) vs. Kris Statlander** – AEW Women's World Championship – Baker retained
- **The Young Bucks (c) vs. Lucha Brothers** (Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fénix) – AEW World Tag Team Championship (Steel Cage Match) – Lucha Brothers won the titles in what was widely praised as one of the best tag team matches of the year
- **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin** – CM Punk's first match in approximately 7 years (since 2014); Punk won
- **Chris Jericho vs. MJF** – If Jericho lost, he would have to retire; Jericho won
- **Jon Moxley vs. Satoshi Kojima** – IWGP United States Championship
- **Miro (c) vs. Eddie Kingston** – TNT Championship – Miro retained
- **Paul Wight vs. QT Marshall**
- **The Casino Battle Royale** – Won by Ruby Soho

### Buy-In/Pre-Show
- There were additional matches on the pre-show (The Buy-In)

## Legacy

- The **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin** match was a massive draw and emotionally charged moment, as it marked Punk's long-awaited return to in-ring competition.
- The **Lucha Brothers vs. Young Bucks Steel Cage match** received widespread critical acclaim.
- The closing segment with the debuts of **Bryan Danielson and Adam Cole** created one of the most electric moments in modern wrestling history, with the Chicago crowd going absolutely wild.
- The event is often cited as a peak moment for AEW and drew strong pay-per-view buy rates, reportedly among the highest in AEW history at that time.

## Reception

The show was overwhelmingly praised by fans and critics alike. Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer gave several matches high ratings. The overall consensus was that it was one of the best wrestling PPVs of 2021 and possibly one of the best in AEW's history.

The event captured a feeling that AEW was reaching a new level as a promotion, with the talent acquisitions signaling serious competition in the wrestling industry.
